attempts.summary: Configured keepalived (VRRP) on node1 and node2 (both OpenWrt 25.12.2) to share virtual IP 10.100.166.253/24 on br-lan: node1 priority 150 (MASTER), node2 priority 100 (BACKUP), virtual_router_id 51, advert_int 1s. Demonstrated automatic failover by stopping/rebooting the active MASTER while node3 (RHEL9) ran a continuous ping to the VIP — node2 took over the address with zero packet loss (62/62 and 91/91 sequence numbers received across two separate transitions), and node1 preempted back to MASTER once it recovered due to its higher priority. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time via native reboot mechanisms, captured pre/post boot_id changes proving each actually rebooted (not just a service restart), and confirmed VRRP/VIP ownership, keepalived service state, and node3 connectivity to the VIP recovered fully after each restart.
